interface.title: Gamma MCA – gamma-ray spectroscopy web application (OpenGammaProject)
interface.field: Nuclear / radiation physics: gamma-ray spectroscopy with scintillation detectors
interface.stage_of_work: Analysing data after acquisition (offline spectrum analysis), with live serial acquisition as a secondary mode
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a gamma-ray counts-per-channel spectrum, calibrate the channel axis to energy with a polynomial, find photopeaks by Gaussian correlation, match them to isotopes in a built-in library, and export the plot or annotated spectrum.

data.note: check_source_spectrum.csv is a single-column histogram of about 300 channels and 10,618 counts. It has broad peaks near channels 22, 146 and 274 (Am-241 59.5 keV, Ba-133 356 keV, Cs-137 662 keV), a one-channel spike at channel 200 that is not physical, and a dip near channel 50. The file has no measurement time, so the app shows 00:00:01. The same file was also loaded as a background and imported in Chronological Stream mode to test those paths.

tree.general: Find out which radioactive isotopes are in a sample from its measured energy spectrum, and save a picture of the annotated result
tree.specific: Import a check-source gamma spectrum, energy-calibrate it, run Gaussian peak finding, get Am-241 and Ba-133 labelled automatically, confirm Cs-137 by hovering (the peak finder puts that peak near 636 keV and labels it Sb-125 or I-131), and export the annotated plot as HTML and PNG

features.name: Click-to-pick polynomial axis calibration
features.general: Turn a raw index axis into physical units by pairing reference positions, picked on the chart or typed, with known values; fit a polynomial whose degree grows with the number of points; check the fit on its own chart; and apply, reset or delete it
features.specific: In the Calibration tab, press the pointer button next to a Bin field, click a peak on the spectrum, type its keV, add rows with Add another bin, press Calibrate (coefficients c1..cn shown), press Show Chart to see Energy against Bin with Point 1..n, and use Reset/Delete
steps: press Select from plot on a calibration row and click a peak on the spectrum (or type the bin)
type the known energy in keV
press Add another bin for a third or later point (degree goes up)
press Calibrate; coefficients appear and the x-axis becomes Energy [keV]
press Show Chart to check the curve against the points
press Reset to toggle back, or Delete to clear
serves_tasks: Fit a calibration curve from reference points with known values
Fit a straight-line calibration from two points instead
Review the calibration curve against its reference points, or undo it and return to raw channels

features.name: Cycling peak-finder overlay with tunable detector
features.general: Run an automatic peak detector over a 1-D signal and cycle what it overlays: the detector response, peak positions with widths, or nearest library labels; tune its smoothing and threshold in settings and watch the markers update
features.specific: The Peaks button cycles None → Gaussian (Gaussian Correlation trace) → Energy (arrows with keV/bin and FWHM %) → Isotopes (arrows labelled with the nearest isotope); Settings → Energy Peak Detection has Gaussian Filter σ, Smoothing and Threshold
steps: press Peaks to show the Gaussian Correlation trace
press again to mark peak energies with energy resolution %
press again to label peaks with the closest isotope
open Settings → Energy Peak Detection, change Smoothing (or σ or Threshold) and press ✓
read the updated markers on the plot
serves_tasks: Automatically detect candidate peaks and judge which are real from their widths
Match detected peaks to known sources in a reference library

features.name: Reference-library line overlay with hover lookup
features.general: Keep a sortable table of reference values; tick entries to draw them as labelled vertical lines on the chart; optionally show the nearest reference entry under the cursor within a set tolerance
features.specific: Settings → Isotopes tab: Isotope Photon Energies table, sortable by Isotope or Energy, with per-row checkboxes that draw dashed lines (e.g. Be-7 at 477.6 keV); the Isotopes toolbar toggle shows the closest isotope while hovering (Iso Hover Proximity 100 keV in Settings → Plot)
steps: open Settings and the Isotopes tab
sort the table by Isotope or Energy
tick an isotope row to draw its line on the spectrum
turn on the Isotopes hover toggle and point at a peak to see the closest isotope
serves_tasks: Overlay reference lines from the library to compare against the data
Check a single peak by pointing at it

features.name: Spectrum plot with display toolbar
features.general: An interactive histogram chart with a toolbar that switches axis scale, drawing style, moving-average smoothing, rate normalisation and an experimental sensitivity correction, plus box zoom with an overview strip, double-click autoscale, a click readout panel and a reset
features.specific: Energy Spectrum Plotly chart with a range-slider overview; under it Reset Plot, X/Y Linear↔Log, SMA Length with Enable, Type Bar↔Line, Counts Total↔CPS (empty without a measurement time), Efficiency; the Click Position panel shows energy and counts at a click
steps: switch Y to Log to bring out small peaks
switch Type to Line and enable SMA smoothing
drag a box to zoom into a peak region (the overview strip shows the window)
click a point to log its energy and counts in Click Position
toggle Efficiency to scale counts for energy-dependent sensitivity
double-click or press Reset Plot to go back
serves_tasks: Change how the spectrum is drawn to make features easier to see
Check a single peak by pointing at it
Correct for the detector's energy-dependent sensitivity

screens_never_reached: Serial Connection live recording (Record/Stop, Console, Show Evolution, Export): no serial ports in the headless sandbox ('No Ports Available'; controls disabled), as the notes said (screens/027.webp)
Print Report output: pressing Print Report opened a new tab that closed straight away and took the browser session down, so the report page was never seen (screens/037.webp is the last view)
Calibration Import (calibration.json): no calibration file was available to upload, because calibration Export produced no file
not_done: Export as an NPES JSON or XML file: Save As opens a Save File dialog (JSON, XML, Spectrum, Background, Cancel), but pressing JSON or XML produced no download and no visible error (screens/030.webp, screens/031.webp). The app probably uses a save-file picker the headless browser can't show; the HTML and PNG plot exports did work. So the saved result is a plot image and an HTML plot, not a full annotated session file.
Calibration Export: pressing Export produced no download (screens/015.webp), probably for the same reason.

Cs-137 not identified automatically: the Gaussian Correlation trace drops to zero just below the 662 keV peak, so the peak finder puts it at about 636–645 keV (bin 263) and labels it Sb-125 or I-131 depending on Smoothing (screens/013.webp, screens/023.webp, screens/042.webp). Cs-137 was confirmed only by hovering at 664 keV (screens/044.webp). Am-241 and Ba-133 were identified correctly.

The app never says outright that the channel-200 spike is non-physical. With SMA on it is marked as a peak with a narrow 4.1% width and labelled Lu-176 in Isotopes mode before calibration. After calibration, in Isotopes mode, it gets no label. In Energy mode with SMA off it shows a 38.8% width, unlike the real peaks at about 10–12% (screens/008.webp, screens/041.webp, screens/040.webp). Telling it apart is left to the user.
Counts CPS view: pressing Counts Total → CPS left the plot empty, because the CSV has no measurement time (it shows 00:00:01) (screens/004.webp, screens/005.webp).

Chronological Stream mode was only tried with a histogram file: it read the file as 1 count on a 4096-bin axis (screens/047.webp). No real event-stream file was tested, and the run ended in that mode without switching back to Histogram.
Background subtraction was only tried with the sample file as its own background, so the Net Spectrum and Background traces overlap and no real subtraction is visible (screens/038.webp).
After the browser restarted, settings (peak-detection Smoothing = 20) persisted but the spectrum, calibration and sample info did not, so the second half was redone from a fresh import.
Not tried, for lack of action budget: X Log axis, Gaussian Filter σ and Threshold settings, File Import settings, Remove-bin buttons, Editable Plot Labels, Theme.
